title: Standalone preview renderer could navigate the host tab

before_fix: Open /preview/?resource=button, create an external anchor with target _self, then activate it through anchor.click().
The direct preview document navigated the top-level tab to chrome-error://chromewebdata/ after the intercepted external request.
The response had sandbox allow-scripts CSP, but the preview was itself the top-level browsing context, so the sandbox could not keep the Site shell visible.
after_fix: The top-level /preview route is a trusted wrapper with the actual renderer nested in an opaque iframe sandbox.
A browser document navigation to /preview-content is redirected to /preview; only the nested renderer is served as content.
Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 probes leave the top-level route unchanged, emit no external request, and report no uncaught errors.

root_cause: The Sites adapter applied a CSP sandbox to the React preview document but served that document directly as the top-level page. A sandboxed top-level document can still navigate its own browsing context.
remediation: Keep /preview as a constrained trusted shell and run PreviewHost only inside an additional sandboxed child iframe. Relay only schema-valid preview protocol messages between the containing frame and child. Redirect top-level document requests to the renderer route. Remove same-origin ancestor headers only from the child response because its opaque parent cannot satisfy them; retain the response sandbox, iframe sandbox, strict network CSP, and opaque origin.

local_validation.sites_preview_csp_and_unknown_resource_b: 24/24 passed across desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 Chromium
local_validation.browser_anchor_probe: top-level URL unchanged; zero external requests; zero uncaught errors
local_validation.browser_popup_probe: zero popups and zero external requests
